children: IPH Limited
has reported an 8.4% decline in unaudited group revenue to $221.5 million for the four months to 31 October 2026, as currency movements and weaker Australian trading weighed on results.
Underlying EBITDA fell 13.4% to $62.6m from $72.4m in the corresponding period, while revenue had been $241.7m a year earlier.

On a like-for-like basis excluding foreign exchange movements, revenue slipped 1.2% and underlying EBITDA declined 4.2%, indicating that currency translation accounted for only part of the reported contraction.

New chief executive officer Tony O’Malley, who took over on 1 July, has identified rebuilding organic growth, strengthening client relationships, and improving execution across the intellectual property services group as priorities.
ANZ Business Lags Market
Australia and New Zealand was the weakest regional performer, with like-for-like revenue declining 7.3% and underlying EBITDA falling 13.5% against the prior corresponding period.
Australian patent filings handled by IPH fell 6.1% during the financial year to date, compared with a 3.5% fall in the broader market after excluding self-filed provisional applications.

Management linked the challenging conditions to exposure to work originating in the US and subdued international patent filings, while acknowledging that the group's own performance had lagged the market.
In Asia, like-for-like revenue declined 0.5% and underlying EBITDA dropped 1.7%, with lower filing volumes—particularly in Singapore—affecting the start of the financial year.
Canada provided a counterweight, recording 3.7% like-for-like revenue growth and a 2.8% improvement in underlying EBITDA, supported by more consistent workflows and cost discipline.
Currency Headwinds
The Australian dollar averaged 70.4 US cents over the four-month period against 65.4 US cents a year earlier, reducing the translated value of the group's overseas revenue.
Its average exchange rate against the Canadian dollar also strengthened to 98.8 Canadian cents from 90.5 Canadian cents, affecting reported contributions from the Canadian businesses.
IPH estimates that every one-cent change in the average Australian dollar to US dollar exchange rate changes annualised group revenue by approximately $2.8m.
The latest figures follow a financial year in which group revenue reached $712.8m and underlying EBITDA was $205.9m, with like-for-like increases of 1.6% and 2.9% respectively.
Statutory net profit after tax rose to $80.4m from $68.8m in that year, while full-year dividends increased to 38.5 cents per share from 36.5 cents.
Targeting Organic Recovery

Mr O’Malley said the board is focusing on client management, business development, and referral relationships, alongside greater use of data and more consistent systems across IPH's international network.

“We have excellent technical expertise, strong and respected brands, longstanding client and referrer relationships, and an attractive international footprint.—the business model is capital light and highly cash-generative,” he said.
“At the same time, we haven't converted those strengths into sufficient organic growth in recent years, and we've lost market share in some important markets.”
The group reduced corporate costs by 13.6% in the opening four months and is also prioritising capabilities in technology, data, and AI.

IPH ended June 2026 with net debt 9.4% lower than a year earlier, a leverage ratio of 1.8 times, and operating cash flow conversion of 110% of EBITDA, while the board has replaced the previous cash-profit-based dividend policy with a payout of 70% to 90% of statutory earnings per share before amortisation.

title: IPH Reports Four-Month Earnings Fall as Organic Growth Reset Begins
